Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- ACME target: 95th percentile latency <= 250ms for standard text-generation requests (up to 512 tokens).
- Throughput: initial target 300 qps with burst to 500 for end-of-day processing windows.
- Concurrency: typical concurrency expected 150 concurrent sessions; peak planning for 300.
- Streaming: you confirmed streaming client will consume token-level deltas; want latency measured both as time-to-first-token and time-to-last-token.

1) Share a short SLO/SLA draft with measurement definitions and exclusions (I attached v1).
2) Loop in Vivek (SE) for streaming/edge routing notes.
3) Confirm internal reporting cadence — you mentioned weekly for early ramp, then monthly.

I attached a draft SLO that covers measurement windows and proposed remedies. Please review and call out anything we missed.

Thanks — looking forward to your notes.

Subject: Re: ACME - SLO / SLA follow-up (measurement details)

Hey Chris —

Great questions, answered inline below. I've also attached an updated SLO (acme_slo_draft_v2.pdf) with proposed wording you can share with legal.

1) Measurement definition:
- "Request start" = time the request is accepted by Redwood's edge (timestamp when we receive the HTTP POST / gRPC call).
- "Time-to-first-token" = delta between request start and the timestamp of the first token emitted into the response stream.
- "Time-to-last-token" = delta between request start and the final token delivered.
- SLOs will be measured on a per-route basis and aggregated to account-level percentiles. The SLA will reference 95th percentile of time-to-last-token over a 30-day rolling window.

2) Exclusions:
- Planned maintenance windows with >=72 hours notice will be excluded.
- Customer-triggered throttling or rate-limit events (where ACME exceeds agreed request rates) will be excluded, provided logs show request rates above threshold.
- Force majeure events per standard contract language will be excluded.

3) Reporting:
- Weekly: we will send a machine-readable report (CSV) with per-route percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99), token counts, and error rates.
- Dashboard: you'll have access to a per-route dashboard in Redwood Console for near-real-time inspection.
- For audits: we can provide signed logs for the relevant window on request (subject to support SLA).

Vivek — can you confirm the streaming-specific routing notes (client backpressure, keepalive expectations) and if any additional exclusions for token-level retransmits are needed?

Chris — if that looks reasonable I'll push the updated wording to the SLO doc under the "Measurement & Exclusions" section.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: acme_slo_draft_v2.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: ACME - SLO / SLA follow-up (streaming & routing notes)

Hi all —

Quick notes from SE perspective: 

- Streaming semantics: our runtime emits token deltas as soon as they are available. We measure the token timestamps server-side at emission. If your client shows re-requests due to network jitter, those re-requests count toward request volume but do not alter the original request's time-to-last-token in our system (we dedupe by request ID).
- Backpressure & keepalive: for long-lived streams (>60s) we recommend keepalive pings every 30s; otherwise idle-connection timeouts can appear as errors. Keepalive failures that lead to disconnects will be classified as network errors and included in error-rate metrics; they are not considered service-side latency degradations unless our logs show processing stalls.
- Token retransmits: if a single request results in multiple response fragments because of network retries, we record the first successful emission timestamp as first-token and the final emission as last-token; retransmits due to client-side network instability are excluded from latency SLO calculations if client-side logs show retransmits.

I'll add a short appendix to the SLO doc describing these behaviors and proposed client-side instrumentation events (request_id, emitted_token_ts).

-Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
